I listed your project's auth configs and posted "hello from dev" to #general as your test user.

**Auth configs** (`composio dev auth-configs list`): all three are Composio-managed, use OAuth2 and are enabled.

| ID | Name | Toolkit | Connections |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ac_e2e0001` | slack-developer | slack | 1 |
| `ac_e2e0002` | github-developer | github | 0 |
| `ac_e2e0003` | gmail-developer | gmail | 0 |

**Sending the message:** Your project has one connected account, an active Slack account (`ca_e2e0001`, word_id `slack_e2e_0001`) for test user `pg-test-00000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000a001`, using `slack-developer`. I checked the tool's inputs (`channel` and `text`), then ran:

```bash
composio dev playground-execute SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE -d '{ "channel": "general", "text": "hello from dev" }'
```

Slack returned `ok: true`. The message timestamp is `1767225600.000100` and the log ID is `log_e2e0001`.

I didn't pass `--user-id`, so the command used the default test user. The output didn't say which user that was, but the project's only Slack connection belongs to the test user above, so that's the one that posted. To pick the user explicitly, add `--user-id <id>`. You can see the run with `composio dev logs tools`.

GitHub and Gmail have no connected accounts yet. Before you test those tools, connect an account with `composio dev connected-accounts link`.
